topics: Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
transcript:
Header: Sep 10, 2026 11:00 AM PT | Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE), Emily Chen (Lyra Head of Data), Rajiv Kumar (Infra), Sophie Park (Security), Daniel Ortiz (Product)

Summary: Quick intro then dive into actual workloads, success criteria, and whether Lyra should run on hosted Redwood API, a dedicated pool, or private deployment behind their VPC. Lots of questions about KMS and audit logs.

00:00:00 - Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Aisha, I'm the AE here at Redwood. Really excited to scope the POC with Lyra. Carlos is our SE; he'll run through technical stuff and the benchmark plan.
00:00:12 - Emily: Hi thanks, I'm Emily. We run a bunch of customer support automation and fraud detection features, thinking to consolidate embeddings and a chat assistant. Goal is to pick something that is production-ready but also cost-effective.
00:00:25 - Carlos: Great, quick ask: can you give us an approximate QPS and token mix for the workloads? That will drive whether hosted or dedicated makes sense.
00:00:34 - Rajiv: Sure, for chat peaks we see 120 QPS at 300 tokens median, but spikes up to 350 QPS during promos. Embeddings is more batchy — roughly 20k vectors per day, 1536-dim.
00:00:50 - Daniel: We also have concurrent KV cache usage in our app; low latency is important for the chat path — P95 under 250ms ideally.
00:01:05 - Carlos: Okay that's helpful. If you need P95 under 250ms for chat at those QPS, Dedicated or Private is usually the safer bet; Hosted can hit low latency but you trade off cost and noisy neighbor at peak.
00:01:20 - Sophie: From security, our default is we prefer VPC or on-prem for PCI-adjacent data. We need KMS integration for keys, SOC2 evidence, audit logs and RBAC. Is that supported by hosted?
00:01:34 - Aisha: Hosted supports encrypted at rest and in-flight, and we provide SOC2 reports, but KMS integration and customer-managed keys are typically available in Private. Dedicated can be configured with customer VPC peering in many cases, but the KMS story depends on the contract. We'll share the security package.
00:01:52 - Emily: What about data retention and prompts — we can't have customer PII retained in logs.
00:01:58 - Carlos: For POC we can configure zero-retention or short retention. Hosted has configurable retention and redaction options, but Private gives the most control. We'll add that to the runbook.
00:02:10 - (crosstalk)
00:02:15 - Carlos: Let's outline success criteria — what does Lyra want to prove in the 4-week POC?
00:02:20 - Daniel: 1) Demonstrate chat latency at P95 < 250ms for typical queries; 2) embeddings throughput and correctness — must match our similarity baseline; 3) stable cost estimate per 1M queries; 4) integration with our SSO and audit stack.
00:02:40 - Emily: Also, functional quality is crucial — we need no regression versus our current model where classification accuracy for intent is >92%.
00:02:50 - Carlos: Great. We'll design benchmark suites to measure latency/throughput, embeddings recall/precision vs your labeled set, and compute cost per unit. For quality we'll run your evals on a held-out test set.
00:03:05 - Aisha: Timeline wise, are you aiming to start the pilot this month or next?
00:03:10 - Emily: Prefer start in two weeks if we can get the legal and security checklist squared away — so bench week of Sep 20 works.
00:03:18 - Aisha: Ok, that aligns. We'll target a 4-week pilot starting with a hosted trial for initial tests — usually fastest to get going — then for main benchmark we can spin up a Dedicated pool or Private deployment depending on results.
00:03:30 - Rajiv: How much setup does Dedicated need? We have strict egress rules; opening peering might take days with security approvals.
00:03:38 - Carlos: Dedicated typically requires setting up a VPC peering or private link; network change window can be a blocker. If peering is slow, we can do an early benchmark using hosted with network ACLs and then validate Dedicated once peering is approved.
00:03:50 - Sophie: For KMS and key management, we'd prefer customer-managed keys. Is that available for Dedicated?
00:03:56 - Aisha: It's supported in Private by default. For Dedicated, customer-managed keys are available but we need to confirm per-contract — we'll flag that as an action item.
00:04:08 - Carlos: On benchmarking: we'll need a ~1 hour run with a replay of your traffic pattern at different concurrency levels. We'll do both chat latency runs and a batch embedding throughput test. Can you share a sanitized sample dataset?
00:04:21 - Daniel: Yes we can produce an anonymized trace and sample embeddings — probably a 10k-row extract.
00:04:29 - Carlos: Perfect, that will let us measure end-to-end token latency, P50/P95/P99, and token-cost. We'll also measure cold-start performance and KV cache hit rates.
00:04:40 - Emily: What about model variants? We're evaluating a mid-size open model and a larger chat model. Which options should we test?
00:04:48 - Carlos: For cost/latency tradeoffs test a quantized 13B variant and a 70B float/quant mix; Redwood's runtime can switch kernels so we'll recommend the 13B for latency-sensitive paths and 70B for higher quality where latency is less critical.
00:05:02 - Rajiv: Do we have to change our infra if we go Private? Our network team is strict about inbound traffic.
00:05:08 - Aisha: Private can be deployed behind your VPC with no public ingress; you'll run the runtime in your infra or a customer-managed account. That requires more ops effort and licensing, but gives full control over keys and network.
00:05:21 - Sophie: We need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM and SSO with SAML. Are those supported?
00:05:26 - Carlos: Yes, we support SAML SSO for admin console, and audit logs can be exported to S3 or pushed to a SIEM via secure forwarder. We'll map out the exact exporters in the security doc.
00:05:38 - Emily: Cost question — can you ballpark cost difference between hosted and dedicated for our workload?
00:05:43 - Aisha: Roughly, hosted is variable usage-based and easiest to start; Dedicated is higher fixed cost but better per-unit economics at steady state. For your QPS profile, if you expect sustained traffic >70-80 QPS, Dedicated tends to be cheaper per token. We'll provide a model.
00:06:00 - (long pause)
00:06:10 - Carlos: One subtlety: Dedicated pools can be configured with autoscaling and burst nodes; that helps during promos so you don't overprovision. Private deployments require sizing for peak unless you run your own autoscaler.
00:06:25 - Rajiv: For the POC we want to see a clear failover story — if a node goes down or latency spikes, can Redwood fall back to a cheaper model or another region?
00:06:34 - Aisha: Yes, routing policies can fallback to a model variant or to another capacity tier. We'll demonstrate failover in the benchmark.
00:06:40 - Daniel: On the benchmarks, how will you measure embedding accuracy? We have a nearest-neighbor baseline.
00:06:45 - Carlos: We'll compute recall@k and MRR against your labeled pairs; embed vectors will be compared to your baseline and we'll surface delta metrics.
00:06:52 - Sophie: Regarding compliance, we'll need a point-by-point mapping of Redwood controls to our audit checklist — encryption, separation of duties, incident response, etc.
00:07:00 - Aisha: We'll send the compliance pack and a SOC2 report link as part of the next email.
00:07:06 - Emily: Good. For the POC success criteria let's list: latency P95 <250ms (chat), embeddings recall drop <2% vs baseline, predictable pricing within 15% of estimated cost, and integration with SSO/KMS/audit.
00:07:20 - Carlos: I'll bake those into the acceptance criteria in the runbook.
00:07:25 - (15:00 minute marker, discussion of runbook details omitted for brevity)
00:22:30 - Carlos: Quick note — there may be transcription hiccups but we'll include a detailed runbook. For the hosted trial we'll provision API keys and a sandbox dataset; for Dedicated we'll propose instance counts (we'll include a sizing doc).
00:22:45 - Rajiv: For sizing, what are the rough dedicated node counts for 120-350 QPS?
00:22:51 - Carlos: Ballpark: for a 13B quantized model you'd need 2-3 GPUs for steady 120 QPS and ~6-8 for sustained 350 QPS depending on sequence length and batching. We'll send precise numbers after we see the token distribution.
00:23:05 - Emily: That's helpful. Also curious about quantization impact on quality — any expected drop?
00:23:11 - Carlos: Usually quantized 13B shows minimal quality regression for embeddings, some drop for very nuanced chat. We'll run A/B on your eval set.
00:23:20 - Sophie: Any customer references in finance you've worked with?
00:23:24 - Aisha: Yes we have a case study (anonymized) with a payments firm — we'll include a reference and a contact if you'd like.
00:23:32 - Daniel: Ok, let's talk legal — is there a standard pilot agreement or NDA?
00:23:36 - Aisha: Yes, we have a pilot MSA template and an NDA. I'll attach those with pricing.
00:23:43 - Emily: Can we get an estimate of how long setup takes for Private? If we need to onboard infra and security, two months is our expectation.
00:23:51 - Aisha: Private on-prem or VPC deployments usually take 6-8 weeks to fully validate, depending on your change windows. Dedicated can be done faster — usually 2-3 weeks with approvals. Hosted is immediate.
00:24:05 - Carlos: So our recommended plan: start hosted sandbox within a few days, run initial functional and quality tests; week of Sep 20 run full benchmark replay (hosted or dedicated depending on peering); if results show Dedicated benefits, spin up Dedicated for the rest of the 4-week pilot; parallel security review to decide on Private for long term.
00:24:25 - Sophie: That plan sounds reasonable. We'll prioritize getting security checklist to you by Friday.
00:24:31 - Aisha: Great. Any other blockers?
00:24:35 - Rajiv: Need to confirm whether traffic replay can originate from our infra to avoid firewall issues — will coordinate.
00:24:42 - Carlos: We can run replay from our cloud test harness or from your infra; we'll document both options.
00:24:50 - (final recap)
00:24:53 - Aisha: Recap: Action items — send pricing and docs, share runbook and benchmark scripts, Lyra to send sample data and security checklist, schedule benchmark week of Sep 20. Goal: 4-week POC to validate latency, quality, and cost.
00:25:10 - Emily: Thanks all. We'll aim to get the data out and the security checklist by Friday.
00:25:17 - Aisha: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with an email with attachments and links.
00:25:22 - Carlos: Thanks, bye.
00:25:25 - (call ends; note: transcript contains occasional mislabels and minor transcription errors)
